title: Point-vs-range detection in MigrationProxy.Update must accept both nil and Time-equal TimeEnd
answers: Why did updating a legacy annotation's time accidentally turn a point into a range (or vice versa)?
How do I check if an annotation is a 'point' when some records predate the TimeEnd==Time convention?
MigrationProxy.Update is mishandling EpochEnd when moving an annotation's time
What's the correct way to detect caller-omitted EpochEnd in the legacy annotations API?
body: Symptom: moving a point annotation's time via the legacy annotations API could flip it into a range annotation, or vice versa, once the new API started writing TimeEnd == Time for points instead of nil. Root cause: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsapi/handler.go:MigrationProxy.Update classified 'is this a point' solely by existing.Spec.TimeEnd == nil, which misses newly-created points that now have TimeEnd == Time. Fix pattern: classify wasPoint as existing.Spec.TimeEnd == nil OR *existing.Spec.TimeEnd == existing.Spec.Time, and treat the caller as having omitted EpochEnd when item.EpochEnd == 0 OR it equals the old/new Time (legacy clients send EpochEnd == Epoch instead of omitting it); when both hold, move TimeEnd together with Time (nil stays nil, Time-equal moves to the new Time). Constraints: only applies to the legacy-API compatibility shim that must interoperate with both old (nil TimeEnd) and new (TimeEnd==Time) point conventions; a pure new-API write path can rely solely on TimeEnd == Time.
applies: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsapi/handler.go MigrationProxy, i.e. legacy annotations API requests proxied to the new annotations API.

search: Legacy annotations API (MigrationProxy.Update in pkg/services/annotations/annotationsapi/handler.go) must detect point-vs-range handling both old (nil TimeEnd) and new (TimeEnd==Time) point conventions simultaneously. Classify wasPoint as existing.Spec.TimeEnd == nil OR *existing.Spec.TimeEnd == existing.Spec.Time; treat EpochEnd as omitted when == 0 or == old/new Time (legacy clients send EpochEnd == Epoch instead). Move TimeEnd together with Time in both cases (nil stays nil, Time-equal moves to new Time). Pitfall: wrong classification flips point to range or vice versa. Constraints: applies only to legacy-API compat shim proxying to new API, not pure new-API writes which rely solely on TimeEnd == Time. Applies when: fixing legacy annotations proxies, migrating annotations across old/new format boundaries.
